sections.title: HID iCLASS Seos + DESFire EV3 + OSDP — the architecture

dataHighlight.heading: Open Supervised Device Protocol — modern bidirectional + AES-128 encrypted reader-to-controller protocol replacing legacy Wiegand for new deployments + secure channel migrations
dataHighlight.text: OSDP (Open Supervised Device Protocol) v2.2 (Security Industry Association SIA standard, IEC 60839-11-5:2020) is the modern reader-to-controller protocol replacing legacy Wiegand 26 / 34 / 37-bit format for physical access control. OSDP Secure Channel + AES-128 provides bidirectional encrypted communication between the reader and the access-control panel, with file-transfer + biometric-template + reader-self-test + tamper-detection + command-acknowledgement features that Wiegand cannot match. Legacy Wiegand installations migrate via PIM (Protocol Interface Module) Wiegand-to-OSDP converters. The chip silicon stack — HID iCLASS Seos (premium enterprise AES-128 + Mobile Access), HID iCLASS SE (mid-tier enterprise), MIFARE DESFire EV2 / EV3 (AES-128 + 3DES + DES), MIFARE Plus SE (drop-in Classic replacement with AES-128), MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K (legacy installed base, CRYPTO-1 broken since 2008), ICODE SLIX2 (ISO 15693 alternate), FeliCa (Japan + APAC public-transit + access), EM4100 / EM4305 / T5577 (LF legacy), HID Prox 26 / 35 / 37-bit format (legacy hospitality + corporate), Impinj M730 + UCODE 9 + Monza R6 (UHF for parking + long-range) — covers every PACS deployment from legacy single-site to multi-site cloud-managed enterprise. Reader + lock hardware: HID Global iCLASS Seos + multiCLASS + OMNIKEY readers, ASSA ABLOY Aperio + HID wireless retrofit, Schlage XE360 + EZE electronic locks, Salto SVN + KS multi-site cloud, Allegion Schlage CO + ENGAGE wireless, Boon Edam + Smarter Security turnstiles. PACS systems: ISONAS Pure Access (cloud-native), Genetec Synergis (premium enterprise), Lenel S2 NetBox (UTC, now Honeywell), Honeywell Pro-Watch, Software House C·CURE (Tyco / Johnson Controls), AMAG Symmetry — all support OSDP v2.2 + Wiegand legacy + REST + OAuth 2.0 + GraphQL cloud integration. Mobile credential (Apple Wallet + Google Wallet membership card, HID Mobile Access + Mobile-Connect, BLE + NFC + UWB hybrid) increasingly displaces physical keyfob at premium properties. Compliance follows UL 294 + UL 1076 + NIST SP 800-116 Rev 1 (PIV in Physical Access Control) + FIPS 201-3 (Personal Identity Verification) + ADA Standards 2010 + GDPR + CCPA. Form factor library (ABS + epoxy + leather + metal + silicone + wood + bamboo + coin / disc) covers every aesthetic + carry preference at MOQ 500-1,000 + USD 0.40-3.50 unit price.

faq.question: When do keyfobs beat cards in access control?
faq.answer: Keyfobs typically win when users naturally carry keys every day and the program values compact carry + durability + quick repeated presentation more than a larger printable card face. Office + apartment + condo + gym + 24/7 unstaffed Anytime Fitness / Planet Fitness model + parking + gated community + self-storage + school dorm all favour keyfob. Cards win when staff need to carry a visible photo ID badge (university faculty + hospital clinician + corporate visitor) or when the credential serves dual-purpose (card with photo + RFID + magstripe combo). Wristbands win at fitness pool / sauna (IP68 waterproof) + festival cashless + multi-day camping. Many premium properties offer all three formats with the same chip silicon — let the user pick based on lifestyle. Mobile credential (Apple Wallet + Google Wallet + HID Mobile Access) increasingly displaces physical fob at premium tier.

faq.question: Which chip silicon should I specify for new deployments?
faq.answer: For premium enterprise + multi-site cloud + Apple Wallet / Google Wallet integration specify HID iCLASS Seos (AES-128 + Mobile Access). For corporate access + multi-site (Salto KS + Allegion ENGAGE) specify MIFARE DESFire EV3 (AES-128 + 3DES + DES). For drop-in legacy MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K replacement specify MIFARE Plus SE (same form factor + AES-128). For LF (125 kHz) legacy proximity-card system specify EM4100 (read-only) or EM4305 / T5577 (rewritable + HID Prox / Indala emulation). For ISO 15693 alternates specify ICODE SLIX2. For NFC + smartphone-app integration specify NTAG213 / 215 / 216 with Apple Wallet + Google Wallet. For VIP / IP-defended limited-edition specify NTAG 424 DNA AES-128 SUN cryptographic per-tap. For UHF parking + long-range specify Impinj M730 / UCODE 9. For Japan + APAC public-transit + access specify FeliCa. Tell us your existing reader hardware + PACS + tier strategy and we route the matching chip silicon + encoding template.

faq.question: How does OSDP v2.2 compare to legacy Wiegand?
faq.answer: OSDP (Open Supervised Device Protocol) v2.2 is the modern reader-to-controller protocol (Security Industry Association SIA standard, IEC 60839-11-5:2020) replacing legacy Wiegand 26 / 34 / 37-bit format. Wiegand is unidirectional + unencrypted + susceptible to skimming + replay attack + cable cutting. OSDP provides bidirectional + AES-128 Secure Channel encrypted communication, file-transfer + biometric-template + reader-self-test + tamper-detection + command-acknowledgement features. NIST SP 800-116 Rev 1 (PIV in Physical Access Control) recommends OSDP for federal + critical-infrastructure deployments. Migration path for legacy Wiegand fleets is PIM (Protocol Interface Module) Wiegand-to-OSDP conversion at the controller side, allowing existing Wiegand readers + locks + panels to operate while new readers + lines transition to OSDP. New installations from 2022+ should specify OSDP v2.2 with Secure Channel enabled; tier-1 PACS (HID, Schlage, Salto, Allegion, Genetec, Lenel S2, Honeywell, Software House C·CURE, AMAG) all support OSDP natively.

faq.question: Will mobile credentials replace physical keyfobs?
faq.answer: Mobile credentials (Apple Wallet + Google Wallet membership card, HID Mobile Access + Mobile-Connect smartphone credential, BLE + NFC + UWB hybrid) increasingly displace physical keyfobs at premium properties — Equinox + Soulcycle + Barry's + premium hotel chains + tier-1 multi-site corporate office. The 2024-2026 trend is hybrid: physical keyfob for the first credential issuance + mobile credential as upgrade option for tech-savvy users. Mobile credentials require: (1) NFC or BLE-equipped reader (HID iCLASS Seos, multiCLASS, OMNIKEY, Schlage CO, Allegion ENGAGE all support); (2) cloud PACS with mobile-credential management (HID Mobile Access, Salto KS, Genetec Synergis Cloud); (3) user smartphone enrollment workflow. Coexistence with physical keyfob during the 2-5 year migration is the dominant pattern; physical keyfob remains the most-issued credential for legacy + budget-tier + non-smartphone users + spare / loaner. Apple Vision Pro + AR / VR access integration is emerging at flagship properties.
